title: Day-2 Automation, Upgrade & Rollback Runbook for Private Deployments
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary:

This document is the canonical Day-2 operations runbook for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It combines: the operational checklist for steady-state, automated workflows for common tasks, verified upgrade and rollback procedures for releases, packaging validation for air-gapped installs, and a customer requirements checklist used during sales/onboarding. Target audience: SREs, platform engineers, and solutions engineers executing upgrades or troubleshooting production private deployments.

Goals:
- Ensure upgrades are repeatable, observable, and reversible.
- Minimize customer downtime and manual intervention via automation.
- Provide a single source of truth for safety checks, SLAs, and escalation.

Owner & Contacts:
- Primary owner: Platform SRE (team: eng-private-deployments)
- On-call escalation: private-deployments oncall rotation (pager: #infra-oncall)
- Escalation matrix: Marcus Li (SRE Lead), Priya Nair (Solutions Eng), Daniel Morales (Product).

Prerequisites (preflight):
1) Validated customer topology: list of control-plane endpoints, worker subnets, routing tables, and CIDRs.
2) KMS/HSM configuration verified and accessible (or pre-staged for air-gapped).
3) Current deployment manifest and image digests stored in the release artifact registry.
4) Backups: KV cache snapshot + model artifact snapshot + database backup stored off-host.
5) SLOs & maintenance window agreed with customer and recorded in the SA notes.

Customer Requirements Library (minimum set):
| Requirement | Expected value / action | Notes |
|-------------|-------------------------|-------|
| Supported OS | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or RHEL 8 | Kernel >= 5.15 recommended |
| Network | Static routing for control plane + NAT for egress | BGP optional for large customers |
| Storage | NFS or Ceph for model artifacts, 1 TB per shard baseline | Validate IOPS against perf profile |
| KMS | AWS KMS / CloudHSM / Onprem HSM | Provide key ARN or cert bundle |
| Air-gap | Installer tarball + SHA256 + signed manifest | See packaging section |

Day-2 steady-state checklist (daily/weekly tasks):
- Verify control-plane health: /health endpoint for each service (latency < 200ms p50).
- Check autoscaling events and GPU pool utilization. Target: 60-75% average utilization for efficiency.
- Review error-rate dashboard: requests with 5xx should < 0.05% of total requests over 1h.
- Verify cache hit-rate: prefix/KV cache hit-rate target >= 80% for production traffic.
- Confirm backups completed and verify restore on a staging cluster monthly.
- Rotate TLS certs and KMS keys per customer policy (at least quarterly for test keys, annual for production keys).

Automations & Scripts (examples):
- Preflight automation: terraform plan + custom manifest diffs to detect incompatible changes.
- Canary automation: scripted canary rollout that updates 10% of pods and runs synthetic traffic checks.
- Rollback automation: safe-rollback script that restores previous image digests and replays KV cache warmup.

Example preflight script snippet (bash):

#!/bin/bash
# preflight-check.sh - run from CI or operator machine
set -euo pipefail
RELEASE=$1
# 1. Validate digests
jq -r '.images[] | .name + @"@" + .digest' manifests/$RELEASE.json
# 2. KMS smoke test
curl -sSf "https://kms-check.local/v1/unwrap" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"
# 3. Run perf profile validation (local binary)
./perf-validate --manifest manifests/$RELEASE.json --thresholds perf_thresholds.yaml

Packaging & air-gapped install notes:
- Distribution: signed .tar.gz with release manifest (manifest.json), SHA256SUMS, and a detached GPG signature.
- Verification steps for customer: verify SHA256, verify GPG signature, compare manifest image digests with internal inventory.
- Example verification commands:
  - sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
  - gpg --verify manifests/$RELEASE.manifest.sig manifests/$RELEASE.manifest
- Offline registries: prior to install, push images to customer local registry and update manifest image URLs. Provide a registry-sync script.

Upgrade procedure (recommended safe path):
0) Schedule: define a maintenance window; notify customer with the runbook and rollback plan.
1) Preflight checks: run the automation from CI and ensure no failing checks.
2) Snapshot: trigger artifact snapshots and DB backup; verify completion.
3) Canary rollout (10%):
   a) Deploy canary using the orchestration tool (Helm or kustomize).
   b) Run the automated synthetic test suite for at least 15 minutes. Key tests: token latency, throughput, correctness on canonical prompts.
   c) If any synthetic test fails or error-rate > 3x baseline, abort and rollback.
4) Staged rollout (50%): expand to 50% and run 1 hour of traffic; monitor heatmaps and P99 latency. Thresholds: P99 < 2x baseline and 5xx < 0.2% absolute.
5) Full rollout: if staged checks pass, complete rollout.
6) Post-upgrade validation: run customer smoke tests and confirm SLAs.
7) Mark release: update inventory and release notes; capture model-variant compatibility matrix if changed.

Rollback procedure (fast revert):
1) Trigger: any of the following triggers rollback:
   - Canary synthetic suite failed
   - Error-rate > configured abort threshold
   - Operator judgement during staged rollout
2) Actions:
   a) Pause trafﬁc to the updated pods (service weight to previous).
   b) Execute rollback automation: restore previous image digests + restart pods. Example Helm command: helm rollback <release> <revision> --namespace redwood-private || kubectl rollout undo deployment/<svc> -n redwood-private
   c) Rehydrate cache: replay cached prefixes from snapshot to minimize cold-start latencies.
   d) Validate health endpoints and synthetic tests before re-opening traffic.
3) Post-rollback: create postmortem, notify customer, and schedule a follow-up patch release.

Observability & SLOs (what to track during upgrades):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per route; abort if p99 > 2x baseline for > 10 minutes.
- Errors: 5xx absolute threshold and relative increase; abort if 5xx > 0.2% or >3x baseline increment.
- Resource usage: GPU/memory per-pod; abort if OOM or GPU saturation detected.
- Synthetic tests: pass rate must be >= 95% during canary.

Runbook for common Day-2 incidents:
- degraded-control-plane: reduce client timeouts to protect control-plane; scale control-plane out by +1 replica per 10% increase in cpu.
- high-error-rate-after-upgrade: trigger rollback if error-rate persists > 15 minutes; capture traces and core dumps to support debugging.
- model-serving-slowdowns: validate KV cache hit-rates and warm caches using cached-prefix-replay tool.

Templates & customer comms (use these verbatim or adapt):
- Pre-upgrade notice (48h): "We plan to perform a non-disruptive upgrade on <DATE>. Expected impact: brief rolling restarts; no data loss. Contact: <SRE_CONTACT>."
- Post-rollback notification: "An automated rollback to version <REV> was performed on <DATE> due to <REASON>. Incident ticket: <TICKET_ID>. We will follow up with a root-cause analysis within 5 business days."

Change log & audit trail requirements:
- All upgrade actions must be recorded in the deployment audit: operator, timestamp, release manifest digest, preflight result ID, and canary run-id.
- Store artifacts and logs in the customer-specific retention bucket for 90 days (default) or customer-specified retention.

Appendix A: Example Terraform pattern (snippet):

# module: redwood_private_cluster/main.tf
# - uses provider aliases for customer accounts
module "control_plane" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/redwood/terraform//modules/control-plane"
  cluster_name = var.cluster_name
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
}

Appendix B: Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Image digest mismatch: abort and verify signed manifest.
- KMS transient failures: fall back to wrapped key cache if available, otherwise pause upgrade.
- Storage I/O degradation: throttle model loading, increase replicas temporarily.

Appendix C: Post-upgrade checklist (within 24h):
- Confirm synthetic test coverage for customer-critical prompts.
- Verify billing/usage counters for anomalies.
- Close the maintenance ticket and attach upgrade artifact digests.

Notes & references:
- See related reference architecture for hybrid-control-plane considerations.
- For air-gapped installs, consult the onprem packaging guide for pre-staging images and KMS cert exchange.

If you find any missing steps or make improvements, update this document and add yourself to the reviewers list.
